Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

anything pronoun

in questions and after a negative

also not anything, anything else?, is there anything?

classical

Cic. Off. 1.101: nec vērō agere quicquam
Cic. Sen. 66: potest enim quicquam esse absurdius …?

quicquam (quidquam)

pronoun (neuter of quisquam)

anything (after a negative, and in questions that expect “no”)

“Not anything” is nihil, “and not anything” nec quicquam. After sī, nisi, num, nē, “anything” is quid (see something).

Examples

  • sed heus tū! quid agis? ecquid fit?

    but hey, you! how are you? is anything happening?Cic. Fam. 7.11.2

  • Numquid, Geta, aliud mē vīs? — Ut bene sit tibi.

    Anything else you want from me, Geta? — Just that you’re well.Ter. Ph. 151

  • potest enim quicquam esse absurdius quam, quō viae minus restet, eō plūs viāticī quaerere?

    for can anything be more absurd than to pack more provisions the less of the road is left?Cic. Sen. 66

Other words

  • ecquid — anything? (in an eager question)

    pronoun · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 7.11.2: quid agis? ecquid fit?; Cic. Att. 2.8.1: quaerō ecquid litterārum

    Lewis & Short: in impassioned questions, = num quid. As an adverb, “at all?”: ecquid audīs?, can you hear me? (Plaut. Aul. 269–270).

  • numquid — anything? (expecting “no”)

    pronoun · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 151: Numquid … aliud mē vīs?; Plaut. Ps. 664–665

    Numquid vīs? or Numquid aliud mē vīs?, anything else?, is the leave-taking of comedy.

See also something, anything, someone, zero.
